lines.en: : Yes?
: Uhh...why is Sensei facing the opposite direction?
: I’m just admiring your new bamboo plants.
: He’s just admiring the new bamboo plants. Are you two done making up?
: I really like bamboo.
: He’s been staring at them the whole time. Nothing else has happened.
: Um...okay. But yes, we did finish making up. And Yuki is going to come back to work starting tomorrow.
: Oh...really? Can I get the night off to go look at bamboo with Sensei then?
: Yeah, just make sure to wear protection or you’ll wind up like your mom.
: No, you can not have the night off. And Sensei will just have to look at bamboo with Ayane again.
: Aww...but she always gets to look at bamboo with him.
: Yuki, get me out of here. They’re going to ask me more questions about bamboo soon and I won’t know how to answer them.
: Sorry, could you turn to face me and say that again? Hard to hear you with you talking to the wall.
: Uh...yeah. Just...thirty more seconds. I really like bamboo.
: Me too. It’s a shame we were interrupted so soon. I wish we could have looked at it a little longer together.
: So, how long you been screwin’ Sana for?
: I have no idea what you’re talking about.
: Oh. I guess you just really like bamboo then because you’re still standing at attention down there.
: I just really like you. That’s from the motorcycle ride.
: Got some bad news for you then, because she ain’t startin’ up and I need to have Nee-sama send a driver.
: Have you tried turning it off and on again?
: Do you even know how motorcycles work?
: No. All I know is bamboo. And also that you apparently managed to extinguish a burning bridge in less than an hour, so congratulations.
: You’re already working again, though?
: Didn’t seem like I had much of a choice. Ain’t no use arguin’ so soon after somewhat fixing things, though. I’ll just tell Nee-sama to play with one of her other dolls tomorrow night.
: I get that. And this could just be me not understanding how cancer works, but I kind of figured you should be relaxing more or something.
: Life ain’t gonna wait for me to get better. Shit keeps movin’ whether we get sick or not. So, if anything, I think shit like this might actually help me keep up in the long run.
: Ain’t no real way of knowin’ until I die, though. So I guess all we can do is hope that doesn’t happen.
: Yeah. It’d be a real shame if you were suddenly just gone before we ever even slept together.
: I don’t think I should be sleeping with the same dude my daughter is. Shit between us is rocky enough as is.
: I’m not having sex with your daughter, though.
: Oh, my bad. I meant “looking at bamboo.”
: I don’t even think your daughter likes bamboo.
: Maybe not, but she likes you. So if you tell her to look at bamboo with you, chances are she’d do it.
: Also, Sana? That’s attempted murder, ain’t it? Girl’s the size of your ring finger.
: Knew you liked ‘em young. Didn’t think you’d be actively robbing cradles, though.
: She’s like the same age as Yumi.
: Yeah but Yumi is tough as nails and Sana cries when she sees pasta.
: Don’t fall for her lies. It’s all deception and she’s actually evil. Also, I’m not having sex with her.
: But you are having sex with Yumi.
: I honestly don’t know how to make it clearer to you that I’m not.
: Right, well, you’ve got my blessing if you want it. Better you than some random Yakuza punk who feeds her drugs and knocks her up while she’s sleeping.
: The bar is so low for you guys that I can’t help but feel bad.
: Just the reality some of us are faced with. Blah blah blah, class disparity, blah blah blah, silver spoons, blah.
: And now you live in a mansion. Oh, how the turn tables.
: Think you been hangin’ out with kids too much. You’re startin’ to sound like one of ‘em and I ain’t really a fan.

: I can be funny when I’m not drowning in sorrow. So take this brief moment of youthful vigor as a momentary respite from the panic attack I’m going to have in the back of a car five minutes from now.
: You ain’t gotta come with me, you know. You could always walk home if you want. You already did your job tonight and I ain’t gonna keep you any longer than you want.
: So you just use me and dump me, then? Is that it?
: Nah, that ain’t it.
: I appreciate it, Akira. Both you and Sara. You guys have no reason to look out for me, but you do it anyway. So if there’s anything I can do to make it up to you-
: Just stay alive, Yuki.
: That’s really all we want. And thinking you owe us something apart from that won’t do anything but accelerate your deterioration.
: So the one thing you want is the one thing out there that just ain’t possible, huh?
: Right. That’s why we won’t ask for anything else. We feel bad.
: And if I fail at this too, can I still expect to see you at my funeral?
: I don’t think you should expect to see anything at your funeral.
: You know what I mean, fuckface.
: I’ll be there no matter what happens. I just hope I won’t have to.
: Let me ask you for one more favor then.
: If that day ever does come, and you find yourself stuck at my wake or open-casket or whatever the fuck you call shit like that, I need you to promise me one thing...
: For the love of fucking god...
: Do not let Tsubasa choose my outfit.
We’re picked up a short while later despite my instincts telling me to walk home instead. I think I might just want to spend more time with Yuki or something.
And while I’m glad that my “moral support,” which was mostly just presence (but I guess that’s all you really need sometimes), worked out, I still feel like I could have done more.
I feel like I should do more.
Sara’s giving her a job again. Tsubasa’s giving her everything. And Yumi’s giving her the time of day, which I imagine is what Yuki wants more than those other things combined.
But what can I give? Because yes, presence is all you need sometimes, but I want to be useful for more than just the space I take up beside her.
I want to be something more. Something important. Someone she sees up close so we stop locking eyes through the reflections in opposing windows.
: So, why shouldn’t I let Tsubasa choose your outfit?
: Because she’ll put me in a fucking dress or something and my spirit will return as a Yuki-onna on account of not being able to rest.
: Aren’t Yuki-onna the spirits of women who die in snowstorms?
: I’m named after snow and my whole life is one never-ending storm. What more do you want from me?
: Fair enough. I’ll make sure you’re buried in black clothes that smell vaguely like cigarettes and tell Tsubasa that you don’t want to be pretty.
: Thank you. “Pretty” and me haven’t ever gotten along well.
: I think you’re pretty, Yuki.
: You’re only saying that because I’m dying.
: Not true. And I’m pretty sure Tsubasa thinks you’re pretty too if she’s treating you like the doll you say she is.
: She’s always treated me that way. And now she’s probably going to do it again until one of us, likely me, croaks.
: How do you guys know each other anyway? I never heard the story.
: Just fate, I guess.
: Fate? That’s a rather mystical word for you. I didn’t think you’d even believe in something like that.
: I’m not sure if I do either, but it would definitely explain a lot.
: We were just kids when we bumped into each other for the first time. Think she was trying to run away from home or something.
: I was still aimless back then. Spending my days riding with a bunch of other girls who didn’t have anywhere else to go. All decked out in leather and spikes and...well, you’ve seen how I dress.
: Then along comes this princess...standing outside of a ramen shop, decked out in pearls and diamonds and a million other things that made her shine like you wouldn’t believe.
: Think she was trying to work a vending machine if I remember correctly. Seemed like the first time she ever set foot outdoors.
: Part of me wanted to just yank those pearls off of her neck and take off to pawn 'em.
: We were all joking about it and shit. Laughing at her as she just obliviously kept trying to put a 10k bill into the machine, wondering why it wouldn’t work.
: Think that’s why I didn’t take anything in the end. I just felt bad. Like I’d be...kicking a puppy or something. I don’t know.
: Guess I still had a heart back then, though. Because I went up to her to help her out while the rest of the girls sat there laughin’ their asses off.
: Think all I did was scare her, though. Second I called out to her, she dropped her fancy ass handbag and told me I could take everything she had if I didn’t hurt her.
: Turned out she got into a fight with her parents over an arranged marriage. Wasn’t even supposed to leave their mansion.
: We hung out for a little while. I introduced her to the girls. Got her name and all that shit. Wound up getting cut short when someone from her family showed up and threw her into a car, though.
: Figured that’d be the last I ever saw of her. This was before everyone and their mother had a fuckin’ cell phone after all.
: She just kept running away, though. And I kept bumping into her outside that same damn ramen shop.
: I swear, it was like when you feed a stray and it just keeps coming back for more.
: The whole “Nee-sama” thing started as a joke. I’d say it ironically to try and get a rise out of her, but...
: After a while, it just felt normal. And draggin’ her around felt less like I was teachin’ her how to survive on the outside and more just...draggin’ her around to drag her around.
: I’m guessing that’s why she feels so indebted to me now. Why I get to live like a fuckin’ queen when all I did was teach her how to use a goddamn vending machine.
: Best investment I ever made, that woman. And the closest I’ve ever had to an actual sister despite all the time I spent with other girls. Funny how that shit works.
: How did you two lose contact then? Why didn’t I know about this until a little while ago?
: Because I’m a piece of shit, that’s why. Because shit that didn’t matter started pulling me away and I didn’t have the balls to face her since I knew she’d give me hell for it.
: Then I fell in with the Yakuza. She got married to some rich guy. And we moved onto different worlds completely detached from one another.
: Which, honestly, is how it should’ve been from the start. I was nothing but a distraction for her. Would’ve dragged her down eventually and ruined her whole fuckin’ life, I’m sure.
: Which she’d kill me for saying, but look at her now. Most powerful woman in the whole fucking city and she didn’t even have to kick a single ass to get there.
: Well thank you, Yuki. Because not only do I know more about you now, but this is also the most Tsubasa has been humanized for me since I met her.
: She ain’t a bad person, Akira. One of the best I’ve ever met, really. You just don’t want to be on her bad side.
: Oh, I’m well aware of that. She just feels more like a puppeteer than a friend sometimes.
: She’s just a spoiled rich girl who knows how to get her way. All of her ways are just a lot more complicated now than they were when her biggest worry was not getting caught outside.
: I ain’t gonna pretend to know everything about her or anything. But I know enough to tell you she ain’t a bad person.
: There’s a method to all the madness, I’m sure. So when she asks you to do something, just do it. Fighting her’s only gonna make shit harder for you in the long run.
: But what if she asks me to dye my hair? I don’t want to be the next Yuki.
: Aww, you don’t want to match? Why not? I think you’d look cute with black hair.
: Do I not look cute the way I am now?
: Course you do. That’s why I’ve gotta be careful not to contaminate you next.
: You can contaminate me all you like, for I am already toxic as can be.
: We’d make a good couple if I was ten years younger and not rotting from the inside out.
: I’m sure Yumi would love that. Then, we could all look at bamboo together.
: Why do you still put up with me anyway? How the fuck have your stupid feelings somehow outweighed all of the shit I’ve done to push you aside? It’s like Nee-sama all over again.
: Well, I...
: I don’t...really know.
: I don’t have a reason at all.
: I put up with you because I...put up with you.
: That’s all there really is to say about it.
: Good...
: That’s the only answer that would’ve made sense to me in the first place.
The car stops outside of my house a short while later and I part ways with Yuki.
And if the gap between us were not so large, I probably would have tried to give her a hug before exiting the vehicle or something.
Part of me feels like that gap would still exist even if I were on top of her, though.
But it’s not because we’re incompatible. And it’s not because we’re “worlds apart” like she is with Tsubasa.
It’s because she won’t let anyone get close.
And I’ve grown too tired of asking people to change for me.
Yuki’s affection has increased to [yuki_love]!
